title: Cluster Design
description: The architectural anchor for a cluster. JSON is the source of truth; DESIGN.md is rendered. Decisions live in the project decision ledger and are cited by ADR ID, never restated. The structure array is machine-checkable: every brief file path is verified against it.

cluster.description: Cluster name, matching the directory under docs/design/

intention.description: The spirit of the work — what the world looks like when this is done. The anchor for every judgment call the documents don't explicitly cover. One to three paragraphs.

problem.description: What is broken or missing, who it affects, why now. Vague problems produce vague solutions — be specific about the pain.

solution.description: The design itself: how the pieces fit, integration points, data flow. Structure and rationale, not syntax — no code snippets or type signatures.

principles.description: Governing principles for this cluster (5-10 max) that resolve review questions before they are asked. Empty array when the project-level ADRs suffice.

decisions.description: ADR IDs this cluster introduced or is bound by. The ledger holds the content.

goals.description: What success looks like, 3-7 entries, each verifiable — you can tell whether it was achieved

text.description: The reasonable thing we are deliberately not doing

reason.description: Why it is excluded; empty string when obvious

non_goals.description: Scope protection — things a reader might expect to be in scope

path.description: Repo-root-relative file or directory path, or a rooted one. A path outside the repository this design lives in is spelled with a root token at its head ($NAME/...), which the ledger resolves from the launch settings of the machine serving the round and refuses by name when that machine set none. An absolute path is refused at validation: it is one machine's, and the same design is fired on a lane's own clone.

brief.description: Brief ID that introduces this path; empty string for pre-existing paths

structure.description: The file layout, flat and machine-checkable. Every file path in every brief is verified against this list; two briefs claiming to create the same path is a check failure.

path.description: Repo-root-relative file or directory path, or a rooted one. A path outside the repository this design lives in is spelled with a root token at its head ($NAME/...), which the ledger resolves from the launch settings of the machine serving the round and refuses by name when that machine set none. An absolute path is refused at validation: it is one machine's, and the same design is fired on a lane's own clone.

note.description: What exists here today and its state

inventory.description: What exists before this cluster touches it. Essential for porting/extraction work — kills false 'create' claims. Empty array for greenfield.

text.description: Specific and checkable — 'sub-millisecond normalization for paths under 1000 chars', not 'good performance'

constraints.description: Things that must not change: security requirements, performance expectations, cross-cutting conventions

oneOf.title: the three-line shorthand

tree.description: The working tree this gate measures: a path relative to the repository root, or a rooted one. A path outside the repository this design lives in is spelled with a root token at its head ($NAME/...), which the ledger resolves from the launch settings of the machine serving the round and refuses by name when that machine set none. An absolute path is refused at validation: it is one machine's, and the same design is fired on a lane's own clone.

fmt.description: The formatting command line, run in the tree with no shell. A tool that lives outside the tree is named at the head of the line under a root token the same way a tree is, so no command line names a machine either.

lint.description: The lint command line, run in the tree with no shell

tests.description: The test command line, run in the tree with no shell

oneOf.description: Three named legs written short: fmt, lint and tests, each at the place the ledger itself runs, each every round. A repository whose gate is these three lines is written this way and is measured exactly as it always was.

tree.description: The working tree these legs measure, spelled the same way as in the three-line shorthand: relative to the repository root, or under a root token the ledger resolves from its launch settings. An absolute path is refused at validation.

shorthand.description: Names this entry gives to requirement sets that recur across its legs, as name to an array of requirements. A shorthand is a name for a set and never a kind of its own: every member is a requirement spelled kind:value, so a shorthand cannot be written in terms of another.

name.description: What this leg is called. An outcome names one leg, so a name is used once in an entry.

command.description: The command line this leg is, run in the tree with no shell. A tool that lives outside the tree is named at the head of the line under a root token, so no command line names a machine.

requires.description: What this leg requires of a place, each spelled kind:value — tool, toolchain, target, lockfile, quiet, place — or the name of a shorthand this entry declares. A leg that declares nothing is refused: it does not default to wherever the ledger happens to be running. A leg no configured venue satisfies is unmeasured by name and stops the round.

cadence.description: Whether this leg runs every round, or only on demand. A leg that answers a question nobody asked this round would monopolise the round to do it; the shape says so instead of the leg having to pass to get out of the way.

legs.description: Every leg of this tree's gate, named. If the repository has sixteen legs this array has sixteen entries: a round that did not run one of them cannot report green.

items.description: One working tree and the gate it is measured by, written either as the three-line shorthand or as the legs the repository declares.

gate.description: How each working tree of this cluster is measured. The gate runs exactly the legs named here and assumes no tool: a tree named here is measured, a tree not named here is refused, and a leg no place satisfies is reported unmeasured rather than skipped.
